headline: Student placed on 7-day remand over 'sniper' comment on PM
summary: Abu Bakar Siddique, a college student, was remanded after posting a comment suggesting a sniper attack on a bus used by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during a visit to Rajshahi.
details: Abu Bakar Siddique, a second-year honours student at New Government Degree College in Rajshahi, has been placed on a 7-day police remand.
The action follows a Facebook comment he allegedly made on a post about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to Rajshahi on October 20.
The post, published by a page named 'The Beauty of Rajshahi', showed the Prime Minister travelling in a RUET bus instead of a bulletproof vehicle.
Abu Bakar allegedly commented: 'Ah! There was a big opportunity. The only thing missing was a sniper.'
The Special Response Battalion (SRB) detained him from his home in the Kachuatail area of Paba Police Station in Rajshahi late Wednesday night.
He is facing charges under the Anti-Terrorism Act, as the prosecution argued that the comment indicated a conspiracy to assassinate the Prime Minister.
During the remand hearing, Abu Bakar told the judge that he made the comment 'as a joke' and had no intention of harm.
The Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate granted the remand to allow police to investigate if anyone else was involved in a potential conspiracy.
caption:
A college student is in police custody after a 'joke' about a sniper attack on the Prime Minister.

Abu Bakar Siddique, a second-year honours student at New Government Degree College in Rajshahi, has been placed on a 7-day police remand.

The action follows a Facebook comment he allegedly made on a post about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to Rajshahi on October 20.

The post, published by a page named 'The Beauty of Rajshahi', showed the Prime Minister travelling in a RUET bus instead of a bulletproof vehicle.

Abu Bakar allegedly commented: 'Ah! There was a big opportunity. The only thing missing was a sniper.'

The Special Response Battalion (SRB) detained him from his home in the Kachuatail area of Paba Police Station in Rajshahi late Wednesday night.

He is facing charges under the Anti-Terrorism Act, as the prosecution argued that the comment indicated a conspiracy to assassinate the Prime Minister.

During the remand hearing, Abu Bakar told the judge that he made the comment 'as a joke' and had no intention of harm.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate granted the remand to allow police to investigate if anyone else was involved in a potential conspiracy.

headline_marked: Next [[election will be held under caretaker govt]], says Home Minister
headline: Next election will be held under caretaker govt, says Home Minister
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed confirms the return of the neutral caretaker government system for the next national election through constitutional amendments.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced on Sunday that the next parliamentary election will definitely be held under a neutral caretaker government.
Speaking at a press briefing at the home ministry, he described the arrangement as a key commitment resulting from political consensus and recent movements.
The minister stated that the Supreme Court has judicially revived the system by overturning the verdict on the 13th Amendment.
To fully restore and reinstate the caretaker government system, necessary amendments will be made to the Constitution through the legislature.
caption:
The next national election will definitely be held under a neutral caretaker government, confirms Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced on Sunday that the next parliamentary election will definitely be held under a neutral caretaker government.

Speaking at a press briefing at the home ministry, he described the arrangement as a key commitment resulting from political consensus and recent movements.

The minister stated that the Supreme Court has judicially revived the system by overturning the verdict on the 13th Amendment.

To fully restore and reinstate the caretaker government system, necessary amendments will be made to the Constitution through the legislature.
